title: Numerical Performance of the Implicitly Restarted Arnoldi Method in OFP8, Bfloat16, Posit, and Takum Arithmetics
problem: Computing select eigenvalues/eigenvectors of large sparse matrices is fundamental to many applications. Emerging floating-point formats (OFP8, bfloat16, posit, takum) lack comprehensive evaluation on standard methods like Implicitly Restarted Arnoldi (ARPACK).
motivation: Alternative floating-point formats promise efficiency gains over IEEE 754, but numerical stability and performance on real-world eigenvalue problems remain unclear. ARPACK is widely used but hasn't been systematically evaluated across new formats.
method: This study tests Implicitly Restarted Arnoldi (ARPACK), a standard method for finding eigenvalues and eigenvectors—special numbers and vectors that reveal fundamental properties of large sparse matrices—when using different numerical storage formats (OFP8 with variants E4M3 and E5M2, bfloat16, posit, and takum). Researchers tested this method on real matrices from two major collections—the SuiteSparse Matrix Collection and the Network Repository—to measure how well the solver performs with each numerical format.
key_novelty: This is the first comprehensive test of eigenvalue-finding methods across multiple emerging floating-point formats using real-world matrices, without customizing the solver for each format.
contributions: Evaluation of ARPACK in OFP8 (E4M3 and E5M2) formats
Numerical performance assessment of bfloat16 for eigenvalue problems
Tapered-precision posit evaluation showing improved performance
Takum arithmetic evaluation: superior to posits, avoids posit weaknesses
Real-world matrix collection evaluation (SuiteSparse + Network Repository)

metrics.focus: Numerical stability, convergence behavior, accuracy across arithmetic formats
metrics.datasets: SuiteSparse Matrix Collection (varying sizes, condition numbers), Network Repository

findings.posit_and_takum: Improved numerical performance vs standard formats

limitations: Abstract only - no specific numerical examples, no performance timing data, limited architectural details
primary_theme: Emerging arithmetic formats for scientific computing
